title: Accountants and auditors
rationale: Purely knowledge-based office work involving financial analysis, tax preparation, and auditing. No meaningful physical component that robots would automate.

title: Actors
rationale: Actors perform dramatic roles requiring human emotional expression and physicality. No physical AI exposure - this is inherently human creative performance.

title: Actuaries
rationale: Entirely desk-based analytical work using mathematics, statistics, and financial modeling. No physical component to automate.

title: Administrative services and facilities managers
rationale: Administrative and facilities managers coordinate office operations. This is managerial work with no direct physical labor component for robots to automate.

title: Adult basic and secondary education and ESL teachers
rationale: Teaching adults in classroom settings is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical tasks amenable to robotic automation.

title: Advertising sales agents
rationale: Sales work involving client meetings, presentations, and relationship building. Entirely knowledge and interpersonal work with no physical labor component.

title: Advertising, promotions, and marketing managers
rationale: Strategic planning, creative direction, and team management. Purely knowledge work with no physical automation potential.

title: Aerospace engineering and operations technologists and technicians
rationale: Hands-on work in controlled aerospace facilities. Some routine testing automated. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028 which was 3.

title: Aerospace engineers
rationale: Design, analysis, and testing oversight work that is primarily computational and knowledge-based. Physical prototyping and testing is done by technicians.

title: Agricultural and food science technicians
rationale: Lab and field work involving sample collection and testing. Some routine lab analysis automated. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Agricultural and food scientists
rationale: Primarily research, analysis, and knowledge work. Any fieldwork is incidental to the core scientific role. No meaningful physical AI exposure.

title: Agricultural engineers
rationale: Design and engineering work that is purely knowledge-based. No physical labor component for robots to automate.

title: Agricultural workers
rationale: By 2031, robotic harvesting covers an expanded range of crops on large-scale operations, and automated planting/spraying is widespread. However, many crops still require human dexterity for harvest, and small/medium farms with variable terrain need human workers for exceptions and diverse tasks.

title: Air traffic controllers
rationale: Cognitive and communication work performed at computer workstations. No physical labor component whatsoever.

title: Aircraft and avionics equipment mechanics and technicians
rationale: Skilled hands-on work in variable configurations—each aircraft has unique wear patterns and issues. Diagnostics increasingly automated, but physical repair work in tight spaces with diverse components requires human dexterity and judgment. Safety-critical nature slows automation adoption.

title: Airline and commercial pilots
rationale: Autopilot handles routine flight but regulatory requirements mandate human pilots. Autonomous cargo flights in very limited testing. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Animal care and service workers
rationale: Working with live animals requires constant adaptation to unpredictable behavior. Animals need trust-based relationships with handlers. Environments vary widely from kennels to veterinary offices to outdoor settings. Robots cannot yet manage the variability and emotional sensitivity required.

title: Announcers and DJs
rationale: On-air broadcasting is verbal and creative work. No physical component for robots to automate.

title: Anthropologists and archeologists
rationale: Primarily research and analysis work. Archaeological fieldwork involves physical digging but in highly variable, novel environments where each site is unique. The intellectual interpretation is the core of the work.

title: Arbitrators, mediators, and conciliators
rationale: Entirely interpersonal and cognitive work involving dispute resolution, negotiation, and legal reasoning. No physical component.

title: Architects
rationale: Design work that is primarily computational and creative. Site visits occur but the role is fundamentally about design, planning, and client communication.

title: Architectural and engineering managers
rationale: Management and oversight role that is entirely knowledge-based. Involves planning, coordinating, and directing technical projects.

title: Archivists, curators, and museum workers
rationale: Conservators perform delicate physical work on unique, irreplaceable artifacts requiring extreme care and judgment. Museum technicians handle installation in variable spaces. The uniqueness of each object and environment limits automation potential significantly.

title: Art directors
rationale: Creative management and visual direction work. Entirely knowledge and aesthetic judgment based with no physical automation potential.

title: Assemblers and fabricators
rationale: Factory assembly in structured environments is a primary target for robotic automation. By 2031, robotic arms and humanoid robots handle most repetitive assembly. Justified at 7 as a natural 0-point increase from 2028 score of 7 given continued deployment.

title: Athletes and sports competitors
rationale: Athletic performance is inherently human—audiences value human competition. While training technology advances, the actual performance is entirely about human physical capability and cannot be replaced by robots.

title: Athletic trainers
rationale: Hands-on physical assessment and treatment of athletes in highly variable situations. Each injury and athlete is different, requiring skilled touch, trust, and real-time judgment. The interpersonal and diagnostic aspects resist automation.

title: Atmospheric scientists, including meteorologists
rationale: Purely analytical and computational work involving weather modeling and forecasting. No physical labor component.

title: Audiologists
rationale: Clinical work requiring patient interaction, physical examination of ears, and fitting of hearing devices. Each patient presents unique anatomy and needs. Trust and communication are essential components.

title: Automotive body and glass repairers
rationale: Each vehicle presents unique damage. Some standardized repairs see automation but body work remains variable. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Automotive service technicians and mechanics
rationale: Diagnostics increasingly automated, but physical repair work varies enormously by vehicle, problem, and environment. Working in tight engine compartments with diverse fasteners and components requires human dexterity. Shops vary widely in layout and equipment.

title: Bakers
rationale: Industrial baking is automated, but the score should be capped at 2028+1. Large bakeries use automated mixing and packaging. Artisanal baking remains human. Score of 5 reflects 1-point increase from 2028 score of 4.

title: Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists
rationale: Highly personal service requiring trust, communication, creative judgment, and skilled dexterity on unique human heads. Each client's hair, preferences, and head shape differ. The social and aesthetic aspects are core to the service. Very resistant to robotic automation.

title: Bartenders
rationale: Some novelty robotic bartenders exist, but bartending is highly social and involves improvisation. Minimal real-world robotic deployment by 2031.

title: Bill and account collectors
rationale: Office-based work involving phone calls, correspondence, and negotiation. Entirely knowledge and communication work with no physical component.

title: Biochemists and biophysicists
rationale: Lab work involves some physical manipulation of equipment and samples, with automated lab systems handling routine procedures. However, novel experimental design and non-standard protocols still require human researchers. The core intellectual work is not physical.

title: Bioengineers and biomedical engineers
rationale: Engineering design and research work. Purely knowledge-based with no physical labor exposure.

title: Biological technicians
rationale: Lab work involves varied procedures and biological samples. Some routine tasks automated but variable experimental work remains human. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Boilermakers
rationale: Heavy industrial work in variable environments—power plants, refineries, ships. Each installation is different, requiring skilled welding and metalwork in confined spaces. The variability of work sites and need for skilled judgment limits automation, though some routine welding tasks are automated.

title: Bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks
rationale: Entirely desk-based data entry and record-keeping work. No physical component. Already heavily digitized.

title: Broadcast, sound, and video technicians
rationale: Technical work setting up and operating audio/video equipment in variable venues and studios. Each setup is different, requiring troubleshooting and adaptation. Some studio operations are increasingly automated, but live event work requires human adaptability.

title: Budget analysts
rationale: Purely analytical office work involving financial planning and budget review. No physical component.

title: Bus drivers
rationale: Some autonomous bus pilots in controlled routes, but most bus driving requires navigating variable urban environments with passengers. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Butchers
rationale: Meat processing plants use some automated cutting, but retail butchery requires judgment about variable carcasses. Score of 5 reflects 1-point increase from 2028 score of 4.

title: Calibration technologists and technicians
rationale: Routine calibration of standardized equipment is increasingly automated, but technicians still needed for diverse equipment types, field calibration, and troubleshooting. The variety of instruments and environments provides some protection from full automation.

title: Cardiovascular technologists and technicians
rationale: Cardiovascular testing involves patient interaction and equipment positioning. Limited robotic involvement. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Career and technical education teachers
rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal work. While some shop/lab teaching involves physical demonstration, the core is human instruction and mentorship. No significant physical automation potential.

title: Carpenters
rationale: Carpentry involves skilled work in variable residential and commercial settings. Each job is different, requiring measurement, cutting, and fitting in unstructured environments. Robotic carpentry is not viable by 2031.

title: Cartographers and photogrammetrists
rationale: Map-making and spatial data analysis performed at computer workstations. Purely knowledge work.

title: Cashiers
rationale: Self-checkout expansion continues to reduce cashier positions, but this is kiosk technology, not physical AI/robotics. Many stores still employ cashiers. Score reflects self-checkout trend rather than robotic replacement.

title: Chefs and head cooks
rationale: Executive chefs focus on menu creation, kitchen management, and quality control—largely creative and managerial. While robotic kitchen systems handle some routine cooking in chains, head chefs in restaurants provide creative direction and handle complex preparations that require taste, judgment, and improvisation.

title: Chemical engineers
rationale: Design and process engineering work that is primarily knowledge-based and computational. Plant visits occur but the role is about design and optimization, not physical labor.

title: Chemical technicians
rationale: Lab work with chemical processes. Some routine testing automated but variable procedures remain human. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Chemists and materials scientists
rationale: Research work with some physical lab components. Automated lab systems handle routine synthesis and testing, but novel research requires human creativity and adaptation. The core work is intellectual.

title: Childcare workers
rationale: Childcare requires constant human supervision, emotional bonding, and responsiveness to unpredictable children. No robots are providing childcare by 2031. Parents and regulators would not accept it.

title: Chiropractors
rationale: Hands-on therapeutic work requiring skilled touch, patient communication, and real-time judgment based on each patient's unique physiology. Trust between practitioner and patient is essential. Very resistant to robotic automation.

title: Civil engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Mix of office-based design work and field testing/inspection. Field work involves variable sites and conditions. Some testing is automated but site inspection and field measurement in diverse environments requires human adaptability.

title: Civil engineers
rationale: Primarily design, analysis, and project management work. Site visits occur but the role is fundamentally about engineering design and oversight.

title: Claims adjusters, appraisers, examiners, and investigators
rationale: Claims processing and investigation work that is primarily analytical and interpersonal. No physical labor for robots to automate.

title: Clinical laboratory technologists and technicians
rationale: Lab automation continues to advance for routine tests in large labs. But many specialized tests and sample handling still require human technicians. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Coaches and scouts
rationale: Coaching involves human instruction, motivation, and strategy. No physical labor component that robots would automate.

title: Community health workers
rationale: Interpersonal outreach and health education work in community settings. Entirely about human connection, trust-building, and communication. No physical automation potential.

title: Compensation and benefits managers
rationale: Office-based management work involving policy development and administration. Purely knowledge work.

title: Compensation, benefits, and job analysis specialists
rationale: Analytical office work involving job analysis and compensation planning. No physical component.

title: Compliance officers
rationale: Regulatory review and oversight work that is entirely knowledge-based. Some facility inspections but the core is analytical.

title: Computer and information research scientists
rationale: Purely knowledge work involving research, algorithm development, and computational analysis. No physical component.

title: Computer and information systems managers
rationale: IT management and strategic planning. Purely knowledge and management work.

title: Computer hardware engineers
rationale: Design work that is primarily knowledge-based. Some prototype testing and lab work, but the core role is design and analysis.

title: Computer network architects
rationale: Network design and planning work that is entirely knowledge-based and digital.

title: Computer programmers
rationale: Entirely digital work involving writing and testing code. No physical component.

title: Computer support specialists
rationale: Mostly remote/desk-based troubleshooting. Some physical hardware setup and repair, but increasingly handled remotely. The physical component is minor.

title: Computer systems analysts
rationale: Analytical work designing and improving IT systems. Purely knowledge work.

title: Concierges
rationale: Concierge work is interpersonal service. No physical labor component. Minimal physical AI exposure.

title: Conservation scientists and foresters
rationale: Research and analysis of natural resources. Primarily knowledge work with incidental fieldwork.

title: Construction and building inspectors
rationale: Field inspection work in variable construction environments. Each site and building is unique. While drones and sensors assist, physical access to inspect structural elements, electrical systems, and plumbing in diverse configurations still requires human presence and judgment.

title: Construction equipment operators
rationale: Equipment operation on structured sites (grading, excavation) sees some autonomous equipment deployment, mainly at large-scale projects. Most jobsites still require human operators for variable terrain and conditions. Capped at 1 above 2028 score of 3.

title: Construction laborers and helpers
rationale: Construction sites are highly unstructured and variable environments. While some repetitive tasks on large structured sites see pilot robotics, most construction labor involves navigating cluttered jobsites with improvised solutions. Limited to 1 point above 2028 score of 2.

title: Construction managers
rationale: Management and oversight of construction projects. The role is about planning and coordinating, not physical labor.

title: Cooks
rationale: Some cooking robots in fast-food chains for standardized items, but most cooking requires adaptation to variable ingredients, orders, and kitchen layouts. Limited widespread deployment by 2031.

title: Correctional officers and bailiffs
rationale: Correctional work involves supervising inmates in variable situations requiring human authority and judgment. Some surveillance technology but no robotic replacement. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Cost estimators
rationale: Analytical work involving project cost analysis and estimation. Primarily desk-based knowledge work. Some site visits but the core work is analytical.

title: Court reporters and simultaneous captioners
rationale: Transcription work that is increasingly digital. While physically present in courtrooms, the work is capturing spoken words, not physical labor.

title: Craft and fine artists
rationale: Artisanal creation involving unique creative vision and skilled handwork with novel materials and techniques. Each piece is unique. The creative and improvisational aspects are core. Audiences value human-made art. Very resistant to physical automation.

title: Credit counselors
rationale: Advisory and counseling work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Customer service representatives
rationale: Office/call-center work involving communication and problem-solving. While increasingly handled by AI chatbots, the remaining human roles are entirely interpersonal, not physical.

title: Dancers and choreographers
rationale: Performance art that is fundamentally about human physical expression and creativity. Audiences value human performers. While motion-capture exists, live dance is inherently human.

title: Data scientists
rationale: Purely digital analytical work involving data analysis, modeling, and programming. No physical component.

title: Database administrators and architects
rationale: Digital work managing and maintaining database systems. No physical component beyond occasional hardware interaction.

title: Delivery truck drivers and driver/sales workers
rationale: Some autonomous delivery in urban centers and geo-fenced areas by 2031, but most delivery still requires human drivers for navigating driveways, apartment buildings, and customer interactions. Last-mile delivery remains largely human.

title: Dental and ophthalmic laboratory technicians and medical appliance technicians
rationale: Lab fabrication of dental and medical devices in semi-structured settings sees advancing automation. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Dental assistants
rationale: Dental assistants hand instruments and manage patient comfort during procedures. The variable and intimate nature of dental care limits robotic involvement. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Dental hygienists
rationale: Hands-on clinical work in patients' mouths requiring skilled dexterity, patient communication, and real-time adaptation. Each patient's oral anatomy differs. Trust and comfort are essential. While some cleaning tools become more automated, the core work requires human touch and judgment.

title: Dentists
rationale: Dentistry involves working in the highly variable human mouth with fine motor control. Robotic dentistry is not deployed at scale by 2031. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Desktop publishers
rationale: Entirely digital design and layout work. No physical component.

title: Diagnostic medical sonographers
rationale: Ultrasound scanning requires pressing a probe against varied patient anatomy and adjusting in real-time. Some AI assists with image analysis but the physical scanning remains human. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Diesel service technicians and mechanics
rationale: Heavy equipment and truck repair in variable conditions. Each vehicle and problem is different. Working on large diesel engines requires significant physical effort and skilled diagnosis. While some diagnostic tools are automated, the physical repair work in diverse configurations resists automation.

title: Dietitians and nutritionists
rationale: Advisory and counseling work about nutrition and diet. Entirely knowledge and interpersonal work with no physical component.

title: Drafters
rationale: Entirely digital design work using CAD software. No physical component.

title: Drywall installers, ceiling tile installers, and tapers
rationale: Drywall installation involves working in variable building interiors. While some automated taping tools exist, full robotic drywall installation in variable residential settings is not viable by 2031.

title: Economists
rationale: Purely analytical and research work. No physical component.

title: Editors
rationale: Knowledge work involving reviewing and improving written content. Entirely digital/desk-based.

title: Electrical and electronic engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Hands-on testing and repair of electrical/electronic systems in variable configurations. Each system and problem differs. While automated testing equipment handles routine checks, troubleshooting and repair in diverse environments requires human technicians.

title: Electrical and electronics engineers
rationale: Design and engineering work that is primarily knowledge-based and computational.

title: Electrical and electronics installers and repairers
rationale: Installation and repair of electrical equipment in variable settings. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Electrical power-line installers and repairers
rationale: Utility line work involves climbing poles and working in highly variable outdoor environments at height. Very limited robotic exposure. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Electricians
rationale: Residential and commercial electrical work involves routing wires through variable building structures. Each installation is unique. Robotic electricians are not feasible by 2031 given the unstructured nature of jobsites.

title: Electro-mechanical and mechatronics technologists and technicians
rationale: Electro-mechanical work in semi-structured settings. Some routine testing automated. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Elementary, middle, and high school principals
rationale: School leadership and management work that is entirely administrative, interpersonal, and knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Elevator and escalator installers and repairers
rationale: Specialized installation and repair in variable building shafts. Highly skilled, variable work. Minimal robotic exposure by 2031.

title: Emergency management directors
rationale: Planning, coordination, and leadership during emergencies. Entirely managerial and knowledge-based work.

title: EMTs and paramedics
rationale: Emergency medical response in highly unpredictable, novel environments. Each emergency is unique—accident scenes, homes, public spaces. Requires rapid human judgment, physical improvisation, and patient trust. Among the most resistant occupations to physical automation.

title: Entertainment and recreation managers
rationale: Management and business oversight work. Purely administrative and interpersonal.

title: Environmental engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Field sampling and monitoring in variable outdoor environments. Limited robotic exposure. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Environmental engineers
rationale: Design and engineering work that is primarily knowledge-based. Some field visits but the role centers on analysis and design.

title: Environmental science and protection technicians
rationale: Environmental sampling and testing in variable settings. Limited robotic exposure. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Environmental scientists and specialists
rationale: Environmental analysis and research. Primarily knowledge-based work.

title: Epidemiologists
rationale: Purely analytical research work involving disease pattern analysis. No physical component.

title: Exercise physiologists
rationale: Clinical assessment and exercise program design. The work is diagnostic and prescriptive, not physical labor.

title: Farmers, ranchers, and other agricultural managers
rationale: Farm management involves oversight and some physical work in variable agricultural settings. Increasing automation of large-scale operations but managers focus on decision-making. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Fashion designers
rationale: Creative design work that is primarily conceptual and digital. While garment production is physical, design itself is knowledge and creativity based.

title: Film and video editors and camera operators
rationale: Camera operation involves physical equipment handling in variable environments, but editing is entirely digital. Automated cameras handle some standardized shots, but creative cinematography requires human artistic vision. Editing is purely digital knowledge work.

title: Financial analysts
rationale: Purely analytical desk-based work involving financial modeling and analysis. No physical component.

title: Financial clerks
rationale: Office-based clerical work involving financial record processing. No physical component.

title: Financial examiners
rationale: Regulatory review and analysis work. Entirely knowledge-based with occasional site visits.

title: Financial managers
rationale: Management of financial operations. Purely knowledge and leadership work.

title: Fire inspectors
rationale: Fire investigation involves examining variable fire scenes. Limited robotic exposure. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Firefighters
rationale: Emergency response in highly unpredictable, dangerous, novel environments. Each fire and rescue scenario is unique. Requires constant physical improvisation, teamwork, and split-second human judgment. Robotic assistance for specific tasks (hazmat, reconnaissance drones) but human firefighters essential.

title: Fishing and hunting workers
rationale: Fishing in highly variable marine environments. Limited robotic exposure. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Fitness trainers and instructors
rationale: Instruction and motivation of clients during exercise. The trainer demonstrates and coaches but robots are not replacing this interpersonal role.

title: Flight attendants
rationale: Flight attendants provide safety and service in aircraft cabins. The interpersonal and safety-critical nature of the role limits robotic replacement. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Flooring installers and tile and stone setters
rationale: Tile setting in variable bathroom, kitchen, and floor configurations. Each job requires custom cutting and fitting. Limited robotic capability by 2031.

title: Floral designers
rationale: Creative arrangement of natural materials that vary in shape, size, and condition. Each arrangement is custom. While simple bouquet assembly could be partially automated, creative floral design requires artistic judgment and handling of fragile, variable natural materials.

title: Food and beverage serving and related workers
rationale: Some robotic delivery systems in restaurants, but waiting tables, busing, and customer service remain human. Food service is highly interpersonal with variable environments.

title: Food preparation workers
rationale: Some automated food prep in large fast-food chains (fry stations, drink dispensers), but most food preparation involves variable ingredients and techniques. Limited robotic deployment by 2031.

title: Food processing equipment workers
rationale: Food processing in factory settings is heavily automated with conveyor systems and robotic handling. Maintaining at 7 consistent with 2028 level.

title: Food service managers
rationale: Restaurant and food service management is planning and oversight work. No physical labor component.

title: Forensic science technicians
rationale: Crime scene work in highly variable environments—each scene is unique. Lab analysis is increasingly automated, but scene investigation, evidence collection, and documentation in diverse locations requires human judgment and careful physical work.

title: Forest and conservation workers
rationale: Conservation work in variable outdoor environments. Limited robotic exposure. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Fundraisers
rationale: Interpersonal and strategic work involving donor relations and campaign planning. Entirely knowledge and relationship based.

title: Funeral service workers
rationale: Sensitive service work requiring extreme interpersonal care and trust. Physical tasks include preparation and ceremony management, but the human sensitivity and trust required makes this highly resistant to automation. Each service is unique and emotionally charged.

title: Gambling services workers
rationale: Casino and gaming floor workers interact with customers in variable social settings. Limited physical labor component. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: General maintenance and repair workers
rationale: General maintenance involves responding to varied building issues - plumbing, electrical, HVAC - in unstructured environments. Each repair is different. Very limited robotic exposure. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: General office clerks
rationale: Office-based administrative work that is entirely knowledge-based. Filing, data entry, and correspondence. No physical component beyond basic office activities.

title: Genetic counselors
rationale: Patient-facing counseling work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Geographers
rationale: Research and analysis work. Primarily desk-based knowledge work using GIS and data analysis.

title: Geological and hydrologic technicians
rationale: Field and lab work in variable environments. Limited robotic exposure. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Geoscientists
rationale: Earth science research and analysis. Primarily knowledge work.

title: Glaziers
rationale: Glass installation in variable building openings. Each installation is different. Limited robotic exposure by 2031.

title: Graphic designers
rationale: Entirely digital creative work. No physical component.

title: Grounds maintenance workers
rationale: Robotic mowers handle flat lawn areas, but landscaping, tree trimming, garden maintenance, and working on variable terrain remain human tasks. Autonomous mowing is a small portion of grounds maintenance work.

title: Hand laborers and material movers
rationale: Warehouse material handling sees significant robotic deployment in large fulfillment centers. But many smaller operations remain human-staffed. Maintaining at 7 consistent with 2028 level plus natural progression.

title: Hazardous materials removal workers
rationale: HazMat work involves variable contamination sites. Some robotic handling of specific materials, but most cleanup requires human judgment in novel environments. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Health and safety engineers
rationale: Engineering design and analysis work focused on workplace safety. Primarily knowledge-based with some facility inspections.

title: Health education specialists
rationale: Educational and outreach work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Health information technologists and medical registrars
rationale: Office-based health data management work. Entirely digital and knowledge-based.

title: Heating, air conditioning, and refrigeration mechanics and installers
rationale: Installation and repair in variable buildings and environments. Each system and building presents unique challenges. Working in tight spaces (attics, crawlspaces) with diverse equipment configurations requires human dexterity and problem-solving. Some standardized commercial installations see limited automation.

title: Heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers
rationale: More geo-fenced highway autonomy by 2031, with autonomous trucks on major interstate corridors. But human drivers still needed for most routes, last-mile, loading/unloading, and non-highway segments.

title: Heavy vehicle and mobile equipment service technicians
rationale: Repair and maintenance of large, diverse equipment in variable settings—construction sites, mines, farms. Each machine and problem is different. Working on heavy equipment requires significant physical effort and skilled diagnosis in variable environments.

title: High school teachers
rationale: Teaching is fundamentally interpersonal work. Classroom instruction, mentoring, and student engagement require human presence and judgment. No significant physical automation potential.

title: Historians
rationale: Research and analysis work that is entirely knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Home health and personal care aides
rationale: Home health aides provide intimate personal care (bathing, dressing, feeding) in unstructured home environments. No physical robots are doing this work at scale by 2031. Homes are too variable, and patients require human trust and gentleness.

title: Human resources managers
rationale: Management and strategic planning work that is entirely knowledge and interpersonal based. No physical component.

title: Human resources specialists
rationale: Administrative and interpersonal work involving recruitment, employee relations, and compliance. No physical component.

title: Hydrologists
rationale: Scientific research and analysis work. Primarily desk-based with some fieldwork, but the role centers on data analysis and modeling.

title: Industrial designers
rationale: Product design work using CAD and creative judgment. Purely knowledge-based.

title: Industrial engineering technologists and technicians
rationale: Technical work in manufacturing environments involving process testing and optimization. Some routine testing automated, but troubleshooting and process improvement in diverse industrial settings requires human analysis and physical presence.

title: Industrial engineers
rationale: Process optimization and systems design. Knowledge work with no physical labor component.

title: Industrial machinery mechanics, machinery maintenance workers, and millwrights
rationale: Maintenance and repair of industrial machinery in factory settings. Some predictive maintenance and routine servicing automated, but troubleshooting breakdowns of diverse equipment requires human skill and judgment. Each machine and failure mode is different.

title: Industrial production managers
rationale: Factory management and oversight. Managerial work, not physical labor.

title: Information clerks
rationale: Information and reception desk work. No physical component - this is communication and data entry work.

title: Information security analysts

rationale: Sales and advisory work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based. No physical component.

title: Interior designers
rationale: Creative design work that is primarily conceptual and uses digital tools. Site visits occur but the role is about aesthetic design and client communication.

title: Interpreters and translators
rationale: Language work that is entirely cognitive. While AI translation improves, the remaining human roles focus on nuance and cultural context. No physical component.

title: Ironworkers
rationale: Ironwork involves assembling steel structures at height in highly variable and dangerous conditions. Each project is unique. Minimal robotic capability in these environments by 2031.

title: Janitors and building cleaners
rationale: Floor-cleaning robots are deployed in some large commercial spaces by 2031, but bathroom cleaning, office detail work, trash handling, and responding to spills in variable environments remain human tasks. Overall limited robotic penetration.

rationale: Highly skilled artisanal work with precious materials. Each piece requires unique design and precision handwork. Custom jewelry creation and repair involves creative dexterity with variable materials. While some mass production uses automation, craft jewelry work resists automation.

title: Judges and hearing officers
rationale: Legal decision-making work that is entirely cognitive and interpersonal. No physical component.

title: Kindergarten and elementary school teachers
rationale: Teaching young children requires human presence, emotional sensitivity, and constant improvisation. Each child needs individual attention and care. Among the most interpersonal occupations. No physical automation potential.

title: Labor relations specialists
rationale: Negotiation and mediation work that is entirely interpersonal and knowledge-based.

title: Landscape architects
rationale: Design work primarily using digital tools and creative vision. Site visits occur but the role is about design and planning.

title: Lawyers
rationale: Legal analysis, argumentation, and client representation. Entirely knowledge and interpersonal work.

title: Librarians and library media specialists
rationale: Library management, research assistance, and information organization. Knowledge work with minimal physical component.

title: Library technicians and assistants
rationale: Library assistants shelve books and assist patrons. While book sorting could theoretically be automated, libraries are not deploying robots at scale by 2031. The work is low-intensity physical labor in a variable environment.

title: Licensed practical and licensed vocational nurses
rationale: LPNs provide direct patient care in variable clinical settings. Limited robotic involvement in nursing care by 2031. Score reflects 1-point increase from 2028.

title: Loan officers
rationale: Financial analysis and client advisory work. Entirely knowledge-based with some client interaction.

title: Lodging managers
rationale: Hotel and lodging management. Oversight and administrative work, not physical labor.

title: Management analysts
